I will keep the land in the wheat and summer maize rotation. That is the system I trust most here in southern Hebei because it matches the climate, the irrigation conditions, and the way I work. At my age, I will not chase crops that need too much daily management or have uncertain prices. Wheat gives me a steady harvest and uses the winter-spring season well, and then maize follows right after wheat, so the land does not sit idle. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable emergence, better lodging resistance, and dependable yield. I will manage fertilizer in a moderate way, not too heavy, because I want to control cost and avoid wasting inputs. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat here usually depends more on timely water at key stages, while maize can often get by with fewer irrigations if summer rain is normal. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and time and fits how I would prepare land between crops. For pests and disease, I will spray only as needed at the usual risk periods, aiming to protect yield without doing extra work that does not pay back.
